transcript.content: Thank you for calling Sky Airways customer service. My name is Sky, and I'm here to help you today. How can I assist you?

"Hi Sky, thanks for taking my call. I'm actually flying economy from London to Rome next week and I wanted to get a better understanding of the baggage policy before booking. Can you tell me what's included in the cabin allowance and how much it costs to add an extra checked bag?"
Certainly, I can help you with that. Let me just look up our baggage allowance policy for you.
"That sounds great, thanks. Just to confirm, my economy ticket is booked on a standard fare and doesn't include any free hold baggage, right?"

That is correct. For economy class tickets, there is no hold baggage included, and it must be purchased separately. You are allowed one hand luggage item with maximum dimensions of 56 x 45 x 25 centimeters and a maximum weight of ten kilograms, plus one personal item such as a handbag or laptop bag.
"Okay, that makes sense. So just to confirm, I can bring one piece of hold baggage with me on the flight, but it has to be purchased separately, and there's no limit on weight for that, is there?"

For an economy ticket, hold baggage is not included and must be purchased separately. While you can purchase an extra bag for thirty-five pounds, there are weight limits. Bags between ten and twenty-three kilograms do not incur an additional fee, but bags between twenty-three and thirty-two kilograms will have a twenty-five pound overweight fee. Bags over thirty-two kilograms are not accepted.

"Okay, that's helpful to know. So if I want to bring two pieces of hold baggage with me, one under 23kg would be fine without an extra charge and a second one between 23-32kg would incur the overweight fee, right?"

For an economy ticket, there is no complimentary hold baggage included. Each piece of hold baggage you wish to bring would be considered an extra bag, costing thirty-five pounds each. If one of those bags weighs between twenty-three and thirty-two kilograms, an additional twenty-five pounds overweight fee would apply to that specific bag.

"I think I've got it now, but just to confirm - if I want to add a second checked bag with one weighing under 23kg and another over 23kg, I'd pay £35 for each one, plus an additional £25 for the heavier one, correct?"
Yes, that is correct. You would pay thirty-five pounds for each extra bag, and an additional twenty-five pounds for the bag weighing between twenty-three and thirty-two kilograms.
"Perfect, thank you so much"
